title: Impact of Layoffs by Big Tech Companies and Support Available for Affected Employees
what_it_is: Impact of Layoffs by Big Tech Companies and Support Available for Affected Employees

sections.label: Tech layoffs questions to Manpower Minister
sections.summary: Questions ask about workers impacted by tech layoffs, retrenchment notices, employment support, past layoffs and job placement success.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower with the recent big tech companies’ layoff announcements (a) what is the total estimated number of workers impacted in Singapore; and (b) whether this will have a knock-on effect on salary adjustment of workers in the tech industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower in view of the recent rounds of layoffs by technology firms (a) whether employers have been prompt in submitting notices of retrenchment to the Ministry; and (b) whether the Ministry can require such employers to work closely with tripartite partners to provide employment support for affected employees, including outplacement assistance programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower in light of the reported ground-up initiatives by the IT community to help retrenched tech employees (a) in the last five years, how many employees have been annually laid off in the tech industry; (b) how successful has the Ministry’s job placement initiatives been in helping tech employees secure suitable replacement jobs; and (c) whether the Ministry will engage industry actors to centralise information to ensure fairer and more equitable re-employment processes.

sections.label: Retrenchment notices for tech resident workers
sections.summary: MOM received retrenchment notices for 1,270 resident workers from tech companies from July to mid-November 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In response to Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Mariam Jaafar, Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Dr Shahira Abdullah’s questions on the number and profile of workers affected by recent layoffs, MOM has received notices of retrenchment for 1,270 resident workers from tech companies from July to mid-November 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Around eight in 10 of these affected workers were in non-tech roles – they worked for tech companies but they were in non-tech roles – such as sales, marketing and corporate functions, and around seven in 10 were aged 35 and below.

sections.label: RTF job placement effectiveness
sections.summary: Seven in 10 resident workers from the I&C sector who took up RTF assistance in 2021 found a new job within six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Responding to Mr Saktiandi Supaat’s question on the effectiveness of these job placement initiatives, seven in 10 resident workers from the I&C sector who took up the RTF’s assistance in 2021 found a new job within six months.

sections.label: Monitoring retrenchments and assisting workers
sections.summary: The Ministry will monitor retrenchment trends, assist affected tech and non-tech workers through the RTF, and expand digital opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor closely retrenchment trends and we will render assistance to affected workers in both tech and non-tech roles through the RTF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will also continue to work on expanding opportunities in the digital domain and invest in our workers to equip them with the skills and also with the experience to seize opportunities.

sections.label: TAFEP hotline for employees
sections.summary: A Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices hotline exists for employees to call, though not dedicated to retrenchments alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, there is a Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) hotline that these employees can call, although it is not purely dedicated to retrenchments alone.

sections.label: Tech salary adjustments and I&C median income
sections.summary: Salary adjustments may be significant for big tech workers changing careers, while I&C median income rose from $5,700 in 2017 to $6,100 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The fact that they had been coming from the big tech firms, the salary adjustments would be quite significant for some of them, if they have to do career conversion or if they have to go to other companies that are not in this big tech space.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Thus far, from the statistics that we have, the median income of workers in the I&C sector, has been on an upward trajectory, with the median gross monthly income, which includes employer's CPF, for full-time employed residents increasing from $5,700 in 2017 to $6,100 in 2021.

sections.label: Tech retrenchment and vacancies
sections.summary: About a third of retrenched employees were in tech roles, and in Q2 2022 financial services tech vacancies outnumbered tech retrenchments 10 to one.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: About a third of the employees that were retrenched from those firms were in tech roles, and if you compare that with the second quarter of 2022, the number of tech vacancies that were available in the financial services sector outnumbered those being retrenched in the tech roles by 10 is to one.

sections.label: Impacted tech and non-tech workers
sections.summary: The proportion of impacted workers in tech and non-tech roles from four big tech firms is about one-third to two-thirds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As I have shared earlier on, based on the data that we have available today and without sounding repetitive, the proportion of impacted workers in tech and non-tech roles from the four big tech firms mentioned earlier is about one-third to about two-thirds.

sections.label: Median gross monthly income
sections.summary: Median gross monthly income including employer CPF for full-time employed residents rose from $5,700 in 2017 to $6,100 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Just to repeat, the median gross monthly income, including employer CPF for full-time employed residents increased from $5,700 in 2017 to $6,100 in 2021.

sections.label: Non-tech roles lower-paying jobs
sections.summary: The switch into lower-paying jobs for people in non-tech roles is not seen as a fundamental issue needing particular attention.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Of course, we are not downplaying the issue and we have never taken our eyes off this at any time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But today, we do not see the switch into a lower-paying job for the people in non-tech roles as a fundamental issue that needs particular attention.
